newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania finmin says revenue intake improves.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania finmin says revenue intake improves.

text.p: Lithuania's new Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Friday that state revenue collection was improving but was still below target.
"The amount of revenue we are collecting increased last week," Shemeta told a news conference, his first since he became finance minister last week.
Shemeta said an average of 18.7 million litas per day was collected last week out of a planned 22.7 million litas.
He gave no comparative figure with previous weeks but said the situation was steadily improving.
Increased revenue collection is a key plank in the economic programme of Lithuania's centre-right government.
The government has declared war on tax evasion, which analysts say is rife in the country.
The government is also working on reducing bowrrowing costs and is to name a lead bank for a $200 million Eurobond issue.
The government is planning a budget with a 697 million litas budget deficit, versus a 1996 funding gap of 724 million litas.
